title: Microsoft Purview: Adaptive Protection retains content deleted by high-risk users (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: Hold: the briefing overlooks Microsoft's published warning that retained SharePoint and OneDrive content counts against storage quotas. It also describes first-time enablement without the custom-setup opt-in qualification, which could lead administrators to assume preservation is active when it is not.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans automatic retention labels to preserve deleted emails and files based on insider risk level.
claims.quote: The integration with Data Lifecycle Management will automatically apply retention labels to preserve deleted emails and files based on a user’s insider risk level.

claims.claim: Adaptive Protection moves users into and out of policies as their insider risk levels change.
claims.quote: automatically moving users in and out of policies as their risk levels change over time

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The documented commercial preservation trigger is the Elevated insider risk level.
claims.quote: In the case of data lifecycle management, Insider Risk Management detects Elevated risk level users and preserves their deleted data for 120 days by using an automatically created data lifecycle management retention label policy.

claims.claim: The retention label applies to previously unlabeled deleted content.
claims.quote: retention labels are automatically applied to unlabeled content if it's deleted by users who have been identified as an elevated risk.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope
claims.claim: The documented commercial locations are SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange.
claims.quote: If these users delete content from SharePoint, OneDrive, or Exchange, a retention label is automatically applied to that content to retain it for 120 days.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationales
claims.claim: The commercial integration retains the deleted content for 120 days.
claims.quote: If these users delete content from SharePoint, OneDrive, or Exchange, a retention label is automatically applied to that content to retain it for 120 days.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Retained content remains accessible for search and eDiscovery in the workload's secured locations.
claims.quote: As a result, that content remains accessible for search and eDiscovery from the secured locations used by the workload.

claims.claim: After 120 days the items become eligible for permanent deletion.
claims.quote: After the 120 days expire, the items then become eligible for permanent deletion.

claims.claim: The retention documentation marks the integration as preview.
claims.quote: In preview, you can use this solution with Insider Risk Management so that retention labels are automatically applied with Adaptive Protection.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The retention label and auto-labeling policy are created automatically rather than requiring administrators to create or manage them.
claims.quote: Unlike other labeling scenarios, users don't see the retention label, and you don't need to create or manage the retention label or auto-labeling retention policy.

claims.claim: There is a single integration retention label and auto-labeling policy for the tenant.
claims.quote: The single retention label and auto-labeling retention policy for your tenant aren't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Users do not see the retention label.
claims.quote: Unlike other labeling scenarios, users don't see the retention label

claims.claim: The integration's retention label and policy are not visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: The single retention label and auto-labeling retention policy for your tenant aren't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The documented retention period cannot currently be changed.
claims.quote: At this time, you can't change the retention period or assign different policies based on the different risk levels, or for different locations.

claims.claim: Administrators cannot currently assign different integration policies by risk level or location.
claims.quote: At this time, you can't change the retention period or assign different policies based on the different risk levels, or for different locations.

claims.claim: The commercial policy is created when Adaptive Protection is first turned on, without distinguishing setup methods.
claims.quote: Custom setup ... If you turn on Adaptive Protection for your organization, you need to explicitly opt in to apply the data lifecycle management policy.
claims.fix: Replace the commercial enablement sentence with: 'Learn's quick-setup table says the policy is automatically created and applied when Adaptive Protection is first turned on, while its custom-setup note requires an explicit opt-in to apply the Data Lifecycle Management policy. Tenants that enabled Adaptive Protection before the integration released also need to opt in.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/insider-risk-management-adaptive-protection and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/retention.

claims.claim: Tenants that enabled Adaptive Protection before the integration released must explicitly opt in.
claims.quote: If you enabled and configured Adaptive Protection before this integration with data lifecycle management released, you'll need to opt-in to create this auto-labeling policy.

claims.claim: Adaptive Protection must be on before the Data Lifecycle Management integration setting can be enabled.
claims.quote: You won't be able to turn on this setting unless Adaptive Protection is turned on for your tenant.

claims.claim: Turning off the integration setting deletes the Data Lifecycle Management policy.
claims.quote: If you turn off this setting, the data lifecycle management policy is deleted.

claims.claim: Turning off the integration removes labels it applied, making items eligible for permanent deletion.
claims.quote: Any retention labels that were applied as a result of Adaptive Protection are removed so that the items can then become eligible for permanent deletion.
